note.markdown:
# Plant exception digest: week of 16-22 Nov

## CNC-04 is the largest loss on the floor
Plant OEE was 74.5% against a 78.7% baseline. Almost all of the gap is CNC-04, where OEE fell to 58.9% from 78.6%:
- **Availability 76.1%** (baseline 91.9%). There were 21 stops coded MECH-SPINDLE (870.5 minutes) and 17 coded OTHER (620.9 minutes).
- **Scrap 6.3%** (baseline 1.7%), costing $2.9k of material this week against about $1.0k in a normal week.
- **Operators are describing the spindle.** There were 7 spindle-related notes this week (noise at high rpm, vibration on finishing passes, chatter marks, bores drifting out of tolerance). In 6 of those shifts, 8 stops were coded OTHER.

The codes understate the spindle problem. The notes and the scrap pattern point the same way, but the data cannot confirm bearing wear on its own; that needs a maintenance inspection.

## Aluminium supply is hurting Aerodyne deliveries
The manifold line (CNC-05/06) lost 1,146.3 minutes to 18 material-wait stops, and 49.8% of those minutes fell on B shift. Operators wrote 10 notes about bar stock not being available. On-time-in-full to Aerodyne Systems is 40.0% for orders promised since 2 Nov (15 of 25 lines missed), against 92.2% before.

## Everything else
The other notes were routine (25), QC sign-off waits (4) and changeovers (3). No other machine shows a material change.

## Actions to confirm
- Schedule a spindle inspection on CNC-04, and decide whether to move tight-tolerance housings to CNC-03 until it is done.
- Recode the 8 OTHER stops on CNC-04 after review, so next week's Pareto chart is accurate.
- Confirm the aluminium delivery date with purchasing and resequence B shift around it.
- Give Aerodyne Systems a revised delivery schedule.
